successors.name: Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu)
successors.text: the Chincha valley: roughly triangular, about 25 km north to south along the coast and 20 km inland

ledger.x: c. 1480: the Chincha Kingdom is annexed by the Inca. 'Part of the Inca Empire around 1480', 'a true territorial annexation' under Topa Inca Yupanqui (1471-93); the Chincha lords kept much of their autonomy and Atahualpa called the Chincha lord 'his friend'. The first Inca expedition under Capac Yupanqui in Pachacuti's…

c. 1480: the independent Chincha Kingdom ends. Its lord, mistaken for Atahualpa for his display of wealth, was killed at Cajamarca in 1532; the Spanish reached the valley in 1534 and the population fell about 99% in 85 years.

wars.name: Inca annexation of the Chincha Kingdom
wars.outcome: Annexation under Topa Inca Yupanqui, around 1480; the Chincha kept much of their political and economic autonomy.

certainty.note: A single valley: the page gives its size (25 km by 20 km), no frontier.
